summary: Feed s177_triple is degraded: NDR on 10 Gbps port is hit by 13.38 Gbps bursts (134% overload), 99.4% of bytes are encrypted exceeding 90% tolerance, and 28.1% of frames remain ERSPAN-encapsulated. NDR is dropping during bursts and blind to payload.

findings.root_cause: 99.4% of bytes are encrypted (threshold 90%), indicating packet broker is forwarding bulk TLS without selective decryption or filtering. NDR requires full payload but receives almost entirely opaque traffic.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR cannot inspect payload for signatures, JA3, or anomaly detection; with 99% encryption detection coverage collapses to metadata-only, missing intrusions inside TLS.

recommended_fix.why: Decrypt relevant TLS at broker (or filter/steer encrypted traffic) to bring inspectable share below 90% so NDR receives cleartext payload it needs for detection.

findings.root_cause: Peak 13.38 Gbps in 1ms burst vs 10 Gbps NDR port (134% of capacity, 2 overloaded intervals). Single tool port is fed by aggregated/bursty broker output without load balancing or shaping.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR ingress drops packets during bursts, causing incomplete flows, one-way artifacts and missed detections; even brief overload creates random blind spots.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2x10G (or more) via broker load-balancing/hash to keep per-port utilization <80% and eliminate burst drops.

findings.root_cause: 2214 of 7876 frames (28.1%) arrive inside ERSPAN tunnel (threshold 10%). Broker is forwarding remote ERSPAN without stripping outer header.
findings.impact_on_tool: NDR sees outer ERSPAN/IP/GRE instead of inner original Ethernet/IP, failing to parse inner flows, VLANs and L7; wastes MTU/bandwidth and breaks detection rules.

recommended_fix.why: Enable ERSPAN header stripping on packet broker to deliver inner original frames to NDR for correct parsing and detection.
